key_insight: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real (RPG) improves embodied robot performance without changing model weights by turning offline experience into targeted simulation practice. It identifies existing skills, rehearses them in simulation with feedback, then transfers the improved behavior back to real-world execution.
problem_solved: Robotic systems are hard to improve because they usually require expensive human effort to curate skills, design rewards, and connect perception to control across many tasks. This paper addresses the challenge of autonomous, scalable skill improvement for embodied agents without retraining the underlying model.
method: Reconstruct capabilities from an offline dataset to identify what manipulation skills the robot already has or can learn.
Build related practice tasks in simulation so the agent can rehearse those skills in a controlled environment.
Use execution feedback and privileged signals during practice to guide self-improvement, then deploy the refined execution behavior in the real world without updating model weights.
impact: RPG offers a practical path to improving robot behavior with less human supervision and less retraining overhead. For practitioners, this means faster skill iteration, cheaper deployment, and a more modular way to enhance embodied AI systems.
